answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 225 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The onyx graph is validated at intake and the yarrow frontier is published, which means the ancestry of every answer is public, and vertex anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Each impostor pays 16 dollars up front. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
